inputs.share_count_basis: 60.9m common shares outstanding at the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (quarter ended 2026-06-27) plus ~0.3m dilutive RSUs/options, Mohawk's steady basic-to-diluted spread (FY2024: 63.4m basic vs 63.7m diluted). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. Buybacks (FY2025 $149.8m, H1-2026 $124.6m) exceed SBC ($30m) and are genuinely shrinking the count ~2%/yr; that is value-neutral in this model (cash returned instead of retained) and is not credited as per-share accretion.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back), FY2025 = $30.0m (0.28% of revenue). Cash taxes on net-share settlement are not tagged in the XBRL feed after FY2020 (they ran $3.5-13.9m in FY2015-FY2020); no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published. Omission is <0.1% of revenue and immaterial to value.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-06-27 (Q2-2026 10-Q; the XBRL feed labels this period 'Q3 2026' -- see notes)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST, Sep-2026) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.3 (housing-linked cyclical) = ~10.7% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% on $1.9bn of notes/CP, ~4.1% after tax; weights ~80% equity ($7.7bn market cap) / 20% debt -> 9.4% rounded to 9.0% because the probability-weighted scenarios already carry the cyclical risk in the flows (bear case is a 2027 housing recession). No scenario-specific WACC: risk is charged once, in the flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost (~$130m/yr) is already expensed inside operating income and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path (treatment B). Operating lease liabilities (~$0.5bn) are correspondingly EXCLUDED from total_debt; total_debt of $1,916.5m is senior notes, term loan and commercial paper only. Finance leases are immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (<$10m); flows are treated as 100% attributable with no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION, routed via dcf-methods row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials' (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Mohawk is the world's largest flooring manufacturer; demand tracks existing-home turnover, remodeling and non-residential construction, so trailing margins are a cycle position, not a run-rate. Statutory EBITDA margins ran 18.9%/19.0% at the FY2016-17 peak, 13-14% in FY2019-21 ex-COVID, and 10.6% in FY2025 (11.3% TTM to June 2026) with ~$76m of H1-2026 restructuring inside them; impairments of $695m (FY2022) and $877m (FY2023) make those two statutory years meaningless. Underlying mid-cycle EBITDA margin is judged ~13.5% (below the 2016-17 peak because LVT/import competition and the carpet-to-hard-surface mix shift are structural), which is where the base path lands by year 6. DATA LABELS: the XBRL feed's 'Q2 2026' and 'Q3 2026' rows are really Q1 and Q2 2026 (they sum exactly to the H1-2026 row, and Q3-2026 had not closed at the valuation date); the latest balance sheet is therefore June 2026, not September. FY0 = FY2025 (last complete fiscal year); year 1 = FY2026, where H1 revenue was +7.4% YoY (largely EUR translation and tariff-driven pricing, not volume) and management calls demand tepid with cost pressure into Q4 -> +5% judged for the full year. Interest income is NOT stripped: the company is net-debt ($1,067m), so the $850m cash pile is netted inside the bridge rather than double-counted. Working capital: receivables + inventory exceed payables by ~24% of revenue, so growth CONSUMES cash (wc_capture -20%); the same driver releases cash in the bear case's revenue decline, which is why bear FCF holds up in FY2027 as it did in FY2020. Capex converges toward D&A over the decade (4.1% guided FY2026 -> 5.2%) because a manufacturer cannot under-invest D&A forever; D&A drifts down from 6.0% to 5.3% as the FY2016-18 expansion assets roll off. Cash tax 23% flat (21% US federal + state, blended with 25-30% Mexico/Europe and incentive offsets; FY2024 cash taxes were 21% of pretax, FY2025 ~33% on a restructuring-depressed base). Terminal multiples are capped at 12x/14x/15x owner FCF (bear/base/bull) per the cyclical rule; Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x, so the cap binds in base and bear. SBC-light (0.28% of revenue): the house/street band is narrow (~$5/share) and is reported, not collapsed.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025), read as mid-cycle nominal growth; equity CAGR is suppressed by $1.6bn of impairments and $1.5bn of buybacks over the window and is not a growth signal here
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-0.4%) diverges >30% from revenue (2.5%) and EPS (-3.8%): FY2022-23 goodwill/intangible impairments ($1.57bn) and buybacks explain the gap, not operating decline. Treat the CAGRs as a cycle description, not a trend.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2020 $1,324.6m -> FY2025 $586.2m (-15.0%/yr) is peak-to-trough on a COVID working-capital release; FY2022 $66.1m -> FY2025 $586.2m (+107%/yr) is trough-to-middle on a FY2022 inventory build. Neither is a run-rate; the decade average owner FCF (FY2016-25) is ~$590m, 5.6% of revenue, which is what the base case converges to. EPS 3yr CAGR is null because FY2022 EPS of $0.40 is impairment-distorted. Interest income is not deducted from the series (net-debt company).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +5% (H1 actual +7.4% on FX and tariff pricing, H2 guided softer); FY2027-30 3-3.5% as existing-home turnover normalises from a 30-year low; 2.5% nominal thereafter (flooring ~ GDP minus mix deflation).
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 11.8% = ~12.3% underlying less ~0.5pt of restructuring; FY2027 absorbs the last $50-60m of charges; then the $285m savings program plus volume recovery lifts the margin to a 13.5% mid-cycle by FY2031, 5.5pts below the FY2016-17 peak.

bull.growth_rationale: Mortgage rates ease into 2027, housing turnover recovers toward its long-run ~4.5% of stock, USMCA-exempt Mexican ceramic/LVT capacity takes share from tariff-hit importers; 5% growth for three years then fading to 3%.
bull.margin_rationale: Full $285m restructuring savings drop through on recovering volume; 15% mid-cycle is the FY2019-21 range plus the savings program, still 4pts below the 2016-17 peak.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3% (H2 pricing fails to hold), then a 2027 housing/consumer recession takes revenue -4% and -1% (FY2019-20 scale, not FY2008), followed by a slow 2% nominal grind as carpet keeps ceding share to imported LVT.
bear.margin_rationale: Operating deleverage on idle ceramic and carpet capacity takes the margin below 10% in FY2027 (FY2023 underlying was ~11%); restructuring savings only get it back to 11.5%, with import price competition and tariff cost absorption capping recovery.

scenario_narratives.base: Flooring demand is at a cyclical trough (existing-home sales near 30-year lows, European construction flat), and Mohawk is using the trough to cut $285m of structural cost. The base case assumes no boom: FY2026 revenue +5% on translation and tariff-driven pricing, then 3-3.5% as housing turnover slowly normalises, with the EBITDA margin recovering from 11.8% to a 13.5% mid-cycle by FY2031 -- well below the 19% FY2016-17 peak, because the carpet-to-LVT mix shift and Asian/European import pressure in ceramic and resilient are structural. Capex drifts back up toward D&A (4.1% -> 5.2%) so the model does not capitalise an under-investment phase. Terminal value is capped at 14x owner FCF, which binds (Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x). The result is a business worth roughly its decade-average owner FCF of ~5.6% of revenue capitalised at a cyclical multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mortgage rates ease through 2027, unlocking the pent-up remodeling demand from an aging housing stock and record home equity, and the US housing supply deficit lifts new construction. Mohawk's USMCA-exempt Mexican ceramic and LVT plants take share from tariff-exposed importers, and the full $285m of restructuring savings drops through on rising volume, lifting the EBITDA margin to 15% (FY2019-21 range plus savings). Revenue compounds ~5% for three years before fading to 3%. The $500m buyback authorisation keeps shrinking the count, which this model treats as value-neutral; a reader who credits buybacks per share would add to this case. Terminal cap 15x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates stay higher for longer, the consumer weakens, and 2027 brings a housing and remodeling recession that takes revenue down 4% then 1% while fixed-cost ceramic kilns and carpet plants deleverage the margin below 10%. Tariff costs cannot be fully passed through against imported LVT, the FY2025-26 tariff refunds do not recur, and restructuring charges extend past 2027. Recovery is a 2% nominal grind as soft flooring keeps losing share. Mohawk's balance sheet (net debt ~0.9x EBITDA, $850m cash) means this is an earnings-power problem and not a solvency one: FCF actually holds up in the downturn year as working capital releases and capex is cut, exactly as in FY2020. Terminal cap 12x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: the Analysis names a 2027 housing/consumer downturn as a live risk, management itself is extending restructuring into 2027 and flagging unrecovered tariff costs into Q4 2026, and consensus is Hold with falling targets; there is no solvency or covenant element, which is why bear is not higher. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs three independent things to land together -- rate cuts that revive housing turnover, the full $285m savings dropping through, and the Mexican tariff advantage converting to share -- and the FY2026 revenue growth so far is FX and price, not volume.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a late-cycle, capital-intensive flooring manufacturer. The valuation deliberately does not capitalise either the FY2016-17 peak margins or the FY2025 trough: the base converges to a 13.5% EBITDA margin and a ~5.7% owner-FCF margin, roughly the FY2016-25 decade average, and caps the terminal multiple at 14x owner FCF because the market has never paid a compounder multiple for Mohawk. Cyclical risk is priced in the 25/50/25 scenario weights, not in the discount rate. SBC is immaterial (0.28% of revenue) so the house/street spread is a few dollars per share; buybacks are treated as value-neutral.
key_risks_to_valuation: Housing turnover and remodeling activity fail to recover from current lows, leaving the margin stuck near 11% rather than reaching the 13.5% mid-cycle assumed by FY2031
Tariff costs on imported inputs and finished goods are not recovered through pricing, and the FY2025-26 tariff refunds that flattered reported earnings do not recur
Secular carpet-to-hard-surface mix shift and Asian/European LVT and ceramic imports compress pricing power even in a volume recovery
Capex normalising to D&A (modelled 4.1% -> 5.2% of revenue) is itself an assumption; a renewed capacity-expansion cycle like FY2016-18 would push capex above D&A
A European recession or energy price spike (ceramic kilns) hits Flooring ROW and Global Ceramic, ~60% of sales
XBRL period labels in the feed are shifted one quarter; if the H1-2026 figures are themselves mis-tagged the FY2026 growth anchor would move
